question: The marked price of an article is ₹850. If a shopkeeper sold the article at 15% loss after giving 30% discount, then the cost price of the article is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

(MP)/(CP) = (100-Loss)/(100-Doscount) = (100-15)/(100-30) = (85)/(70)

MP = ₹850 → 85 units = ₹850 → 1 unit = ₹10

Thus, CP = 70 × 10 = ₹700

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

The marked price of an article is ₹850

Article is sold at 15% loss after giving a 30% discount

Concept used:

SP = MP × ((100-Discount)/(100))

SP = CP × ((100-Loss)/(100))

Calculation:

SP = 850 × (100-30)/(100) = 850 × (70)/(100) = Rs 595

CP = 595 × (100)/(100-15) = 595 × (100)/(85) = Rs 700

∴ The CP of the article is Rs 700.
